# Independent review: boundary energy and causal reconstruction

Verdict: **ACCEPT_BOUNDARY_ENERGY_CAUSALITY_MAP_ONLY**.

Reviewed final candidate: `CAUSAL_RECONSTRUCTION_CANDIDATE.md`, SHA256 `d203e0437b1125b1603156c3dc3e3e8ccd59a2028513ca9869c175cbf2a38a09`, 11067 bytes, 206 LF. The complete final file was read. This review accepts the bounded analytic statements A0–A5 and their stated limitations. It does not establish causality of the actual theta response, the old condition P, positivity of the original signed field/Q/V, or RH. It supplies no canonical admission or formal Lean result.

The two requested corrections from the first draft are present: A4 now gives the positive atomic source and its mass 3 explicitly; A5 limits the negative control to positivity/evenness of a measure and explicitly excludes a test of smooth strict positivity or the theta/PF assumptions. These are substantive scope clarifications, not changes to the multiplier or witness formulas. No further correction is required for this acceptance.

## 1. Exact inputs and source fidelity

All hashes below were checked against local bytes. Source locations are in the same private staging directory unless a project-relative path is given.

The project inputs were read in the isolated `gamma-reciprocity-worktree`, not modified. I checked the source definitions and complete OPENSGN Lemma 7 with (27)–(29), the analytic Poisson continuation and zero consequence, the control/scope discussion, and the independent check. The latter's numerical observations are historical diagnostics; they are neither evidence of P nor used in this acceptance.

Lall's version 2001.10.17.01, slides 6-23/6-24, supplies the bounded half-line causal LTI/H-infinity correspondence with the right-half-plane convention used here. This is lecture-note background, not a new theorem about the theta source. The specified quote and the two directions of the correspondence match the supplied pages.

Luger–Ou, published Part I, section 2.6, Definition 4 and Theorem 8, printed p.444/PDF p.12, uses cumulative work at every finite cutoff for every compact smooth input. The conjugation in its work integral was checked on the rendered page, rather than inferred from the text extraction. Its real passive-convolution correspondence is with a symmetric Herglotz function after the stated rotation: for a Laplace response W, f(z)=iW(z/i). Equivalently, the right-half-plane response is positive real. The candidate uses this only conditionally and does not replace cumulative work by whole-line work. Both primary key-page PNGs were visually read.

The named classical inputs are these correspondence theorems, Plancherel, bounded harmonic uniqueness, and local Hardy boundary uniqueness. The candidate's applications pay the relevant domains and boundedness; it does not claim to reprove all the classical background.

## 2. A0–A1: exact boundary multiplier and total energy

The sign conventions are consistent. Since X is even, F(iy)=X(-y)=X(y), while F'(iy)=iX'(-y)=-iX'(y). Thus M(iy)=X(y)/(X(y)-iX'(y)). Multiplying by the conjugate denominator gives m=omega+i eta with precisely the definitions in A0, and |m|^2=Re m=omega in [0,1]. Real even X has odd real derivative, hence m(-y)=conjugate(m(y)).

A real zero of X of multiplicity k is removable for this ratio: the denominator has order k-1 and the numerator order k. In particular the ratio tends to zero. Such points are isolated and make no difference to the multiplier as an L-infinity equivalence class. X is not identically zero, so the common real zero set has measure zero. Nothing here assumes simple zeros or RH.

The inverse Fourier transform of the bounded function m is a real tempered distribution. The associated multiplier R is a bounded whole-line L2 contraction. Convolution with that distribution agrees with the multiplier on Schwartz inputs and extends to L2 by boundedness; one need not define the convolution of an arbitrary pair of distributions.

For the Fourier convention in A0, Plancherel has factor 1/(2pi), giving exactly

    Re <u,Ru> = (1/(2pi)) integral omega |uhat|^2 = ||Ru||_2^2.

Every expression is finite for u in complex L2. Moreover |2m-1|=1 a.e.; multiplication by its conjugate is the bounded inverse, so U=2R-I is unitary, not merely an isometry. These statements depend only on real-axis algebra. They make no identification of ||Ru|| with the old signed-field norm or the original Q/V.

## 3. A2: complete cutoff equivalence and its support meaning

Set a=P_Tu and b=(I-P_T)u. Then

    W_T(u) = Re <a,Ra> + Re <a,Rb>
           = ||Ra||^2 + Re <a,P_T Rb>.

The first norm is on the whole output line, as the candidate explicitly states. No projection is commuted through R, and no outgoing boundary energy is silently discarded.

For each fixed T the displayed real quadratic form is continuous on complex L2. Therefore nonnegativity on compact smooth inputs extends by density to all L2 inputs. Conversely the restriction is immediate. If P_T R(I-P_T)=0 the cross term vanishes and the claimed sign follows.

If that block is nonzero, choose b supported after T with P_T Rb nonzero and take a=P_T Rb. Then <a,Rb>=||P_T Rb||^2>0. For u=a+lambda b a sufficiently negative real lambda makes W_T negative. More generally the complex-lambda argument in the candidate is valid with the convention conjugating the first argument. There is no quadratic |lambda|^2 term to obstruct the argument. Thus (a), (b), and (c) are genuinely equivalent, including complex test inputs. A strict L2 violation can also be approximated by compact smooth inputs while preserving its sign.

For a translation-invariant distribution convolution, this no-future-to-past condition is equivalent to support Y contained in [0,infinity). The forward implication follows first for compact smooth future inputs by support addition, then by bounded L2 approximation. For the reverse implication, apply the no-future-to-past property to an approximate identity supported in (0,epsilon); Y convolved with it vanishes before 0, and these convolutions converge to Y in distributions. Thus Y vanishes on the negative half-line. An atom at 0 is allowed, and the choice of whether the cutoff contains its endpoint has no effect in L2.

The absence of a useful small-norm replacement is exact: any nonzero cross block can be amplified by the arbitrarily large later input coefficient. A2 proves an equivalent support requirement; it does not prove that requirement for the actual multiplier.

## 4. A3: conditional Hardy reconstruction of the original M

Assume the support condition, only for this paragraph's implication. Restrict R to L2 inputs supported in [0,infinity). Its outputs have that support; the restriction is bounded and commutes with the right-shift semigroup, as follows from whole-line translation invariance. These are the hypotheses of the Lall correspondence. It produces G in H-infinity on Re p>0 with boundary values m a.e. and norm at most 1.

The old Omega is holomorphic in the right half-plane using the symmetrized kernel p/(p^2+y^2), whose tails are O(y^-2) locally uniformly in p. For p=x+it and even omega, taking real parts and combining the two poles of that kernel gives the ordinary Poisson integral

    Re Omega(x+it) = (1/pi) integral x omega(y)/(x^2+(t-y)^2) dy.

In particular this real part is bounded between 0 and 1. The bounded harmonic real part of G has boundary omega, so bounded harmonic uniqueness gives Re G=Re Omega. This step does not assume that the original meromorphic M has a bounded analytic continuation; nor does it need to assume an a priori bound for Im Omega. A possible uncontrolled linear harmonic term at infinity is excluded by boundedness of the harmonic real part.

The holomorphic difference G-Omega is therefore an imaginary constant. The real convolution symmetry implies G(conjugate p)=conjugate G(p) by uniqueness of the H-infinity transfer function (the reflected function has the same boundary data). Omega is real on the positive real axis directly from its integral. The constant is zero.

The next identification with M is necessary and correct. A suitable boundary neighborhood exists already at p=0: F(0)=xi(1/2)>0 and F'(0)=0. Hence F+F' is nonzero on a small disk around 0, and M is holomorphic and bounded on a smaller closed disk. On its right half-disk, G-M is bounded analytic and has zero a.e. boundary values on the straight edge. Local Hardy uniqueness forces it to vanish. This is an application with the boundedness hypothesis paid, not the invalid assertion that arbitrary meromorphic functions are determined by an uncontrolled boundary trace.

Finally (F+F')G-F is holomorphic on the connected right half-plane and vanishes on that open half-disk. The identity theorem makes it zero everywhere, without division at any hypothetical interior denominator zeros. Together with G=Omega this gives the old P on the required real ray. On that ray the earlier source supplies the legitimate positive denominator. No global growth estimate for M has been assumed to bypass this argument.

The prior OPENSGN Lemma 7 is the consumer being recovered. This is a conditional route to that existing condition, not a new weaker hypothesis, a newly proved Poisson identity, or an additional norm formula for R. The prior report uses the other convention for which slot of the inner product is linear; all comparisons here involve the real work or the scalar condition P, so this convention change introduces no sign discrepancy.

The Luger–Ou input is also used within its proper domain: compact smooth inputs give locally L2 and hence locally integrable outputs; the distribution is real and tempered. The unpaid hypothesis is exactly cumulative work for every cutoff, equivalent to the support condition by A2. Neither source permits that hypothesis to be inferred from A1 alone.

## 5. A4: explicit non-theta control and exact smooth witness

For X0(z)=2+cos(4z), F0(p)=2+cosh(4p), put z=exp(4p). Direct calculation gives

    F0=(z^2+4z+1)/(2z),  F0'=(4z^2-4)/(2z),
    M0=(z^2+4z+1)/(5z^2+4z-3).

With s=sqrt(19), a=(-2+s)/5, b=(-2-s)/5, the denominator is 5(z-a)(z-b), 0<a<1, b<-1. Its residues are A=4(2s+1)/(25s) and B=4(2s-1)/(25s), both positive; its constant polynomial part is 1/5. Thus (4) is exact. There is no cancellation at b because B is nonzero.

On the unit circle, expansion of A/(z-a) in negative powers and B/(z-b) in nonnegative powers is absolutely and uniformly convergent. The latter's constant contribution is -B/b. Hence (5), d0=1/5-B/b>0, and d1=-B/b^2<0 are exact. Under the specified Fourier convention, exp(-4iny) corresponds to delta at +4n and exp(4iny) to delta at -4n. Both geometric coefficient series are absolutely summable; Y0 is a finite signed measure, with the asserted nonzero negative-time atom. The listed poles over exp(4p)=b have real part log|b|/4>0 and are uncancelled.

For the smooth witness, u=v+lambda v(t-4), epsilon<1 and T=2 imply P_Tu=v. On the support of v, the central atom acting on v and the atom at -4 acting on the later copy are the only contributions: every other shift misses both supports. The stated lambda=-2d0/d1>0 therefore gives

    W_2(u)=(d0+lambda d1)||v||^2=-d0||v||^2<0.

All functions used for this witness are actual compact smooth inputs; no delta input approximation is required. A1 nevertheless gives whole-line work ||R0u||^2>=0. This is a strict analytic finite-cutoff witness for this control, not a numerical indication and not a witness against actual theta V.

The final source qualification is correct. The inverse Fourier source is 2 delta_0+(delta_4+delta_-4)/2 with total mass 3; division by 3 produces a probability measure without changing M0. X0 is positive on the real axis, even and real; F0 and F0' are positive for positive real p; X0 has nonreal zeros. These facts refute the generic assertion from those measure-level/algebraic conditions to passivity. They do not refute a theorem additionally assuming a smooth strictly positive density, theta reciprocity, or additive PF-infinity. Omitting the old smooth factor B is explicitly disclosed and no property of that factor is imported.

## 6. A5: unchanged full-source convolution and uniqueness scope

For the pinned full theta normalization, q=Phi/xi(1/2) has Fourier transform X/xi(1/2). The full source is even, positive and rapidly decreasing with its required derivatives, so q and a_q=(1-t)q are Schwartz. Since Fourier-minus sends t q to i times the derivative of qhat,

    ahat_q=(X-iX')/xi(1/2).

There is no missing minus sign, character shift, or 2pi factor. The distribution convolution a_q*Y is defined, and its Fourier transform is the product ahat_q m=qhat. This proves exactly (7) for the unmodified source and the original boundary response.

Uniqueness asserted in A5 is correctly restricted to bounded measurable multiplier solutions modulo null sets. The denominator can vanish on the real axis only at common zeros of real X and X', an isolated set of measure zero. Thus division gives uniqueness almost everywhere. This does not assert uniqueness among all tempered distribution solutions: distributions supported at denominator zeros would require a separate analysis and are outside the claim.

The equation has already been solved on the whole line. Its solution's one-sided support is a further assertion and remains open. Also a_q itself has the factor 1-t and is not a nonnegative renewal kernel; positivity of q does not silently supply a positive inversion theorem. No additive PF property is transferred from a different carrier r to q. Final A5 correctly limits the negative control to measure-level positivity/evenness and leaves smooth strict positivity and the theta/PF hypotheses untested by that control.

## 7. Accepted scope and stopping point

Accepted statements are the unconditional bounded-multiplier/total-energy identity; the all-complex, all-cutoff equivalence to causality for this R; the conditional identification of a causal H-infinity extension with the actual meromorphic M and thus old OPENSGN P; the explicit analytic control and smooth negative-cutoff witness; and the exact full-source convolution equation with its limited uniqueness statement.

The mathematical content is a domain/alias and method-boundary audit. There is no new positive supplier for the full source. In particular no acceptance is given to actual causality, P, a signed-field norm identity, original Q/V positivity, or RH. Neither a pole of the control nor its negative cumulative work is a counterexample to those theta-source targets. The review does not certify search freshness, provider state, or canonical lifecycle; the candidate's search-receipt narrative is not mathematical evidence and was not used in the proofs checked here.

The final instruction to stop the generic passivity/Hardy hunt at this existing open premise is consistent with the result. Reissuing 'prove causality' without a new source-specific mechanism would rename the same obstruction. This review writes only its assigned private file and authorizes no new dispatch, canonical mutation, publication or sign-counter change.
